editors-message.title: Clear Skies ahead
editors-message.byline: Caitlin Bernal and Gabriel Renee Quizan
editors-message.article:
SOARING ABOVE lofty expectations, the Ateneo Blue Eagles showcased a series of outstanding and historic performances in the first semester of the University Athletic Association of the Philippines’ (UAAP) Season 88. Across a nine-sport schedule, the Blue and White brought home eight podium finishes and three championships—a testament to the exemplary caliber embodied forth by the University’s student-athletes.

With the UAAP gearing up for a packed second-semester slate, the Blue Eagles look to end Season 88 on a high note as they carry the Ateneo banner with beaming pride and fiery resolve.

The second installment of Season 88 will follow 20 teams on 20 different journeys, all united by a single goal of reaching the UAAP pinnacle. This semester’s primer aims to reemphasize the collective drive and passion embodied by the Blue Eagles.

As the dedication to attaining greatness intensifies in Loyola Heights, The GUIDON Sports remains an attentive chronicler of the unique Atenean sportsperson journey. From the Blue Eagles’ pursuit of knowledge in the classroom to their zeal for athletic mastery, the publication stays committed to being the voice of Blue Eagle excellence.

As our student-athletes strive to scale daring heights, let us, the Ateneo community, rally with them in every fight, fall, and victory.

mens-basketball.title: Rising Above
mens-basketball.article:
FOLLOWING A tough UAAP Season 87 showing, the Ateneo Men’s 3x3 Basketball Team looks to turn the page after their one-win campaign.

With second-year Head Coach and former Ateneo standout Nico Salva, the Blue Eagles continue their mission of building a more competitive program for the upcoming season. This mission was reflected in last season’s squad, composed of Andre Tan, Danger Tupas, Adam Dela Cruz, and Sam Reyes.

For Season 88, Ateneo aims to showcase the lessons that they have learned and embrace the growth from last season’s challenges. Repping the court this time around will be Team A mainstays Shawn Tuano, Drew Bongo, Kyle Gamber, and Thirdy Ebdane.

As 3x3 basketball continues to rise in popularity, the Katipunan-based unit remains determined to reclaim their place at the top of the sport in the UAAP arena. With a renewed focus and sense of teamwork, the Blue Eagles are ready to soar and get buckets this Season 88.

Editor’s Note: The publication has chosen to feature Head Coach Nico Salva in lieu of a team captain, with the finalization of the Men’s 3x3 Basketball roster still in progress prior to the completion of the primer.

womens-basketball.title: The gold standard
womens-basketball.article:
SHOCKING THE UAAP basketball scene with their Cinderella first-place finish in Season 87, the Ateneo Women’s 3x3 Basketball Team sets their sight on a repeat title in Season 88 to prove that their breakthrough was no fluke.

After capturing their first-ever gold medal finish in last year’s competition, Head Coach PJ Navarro, alongside confirmed returnees Kai Oani and Lauren Lopez, are back in tow in pursuit of a back-to-back championship.

The Blue and White enters the season eager to deliver another impressive showing under Head Coach Navarro. As defending champions, the Blue Eagles embrace both the challenge of heightened expectations and the pressures that come with it.

Following their narrow exit in the semifinals on the 5-on-5 stage, Ateneo’s perennial 3x3 squad is intent on reasserting their place among the UAAP’s elite.

That focus now shifts to the 3x3 circuit, where belief forged in gold and resolve strengthened by adversity fuel the Katipunan-based squad’s bid to remain the gold standard of the Women’s division.

Editor’s Note: The publication has chosen to feature Head Coach PJ Navarro in lieu of a team captain, with the finalization of the Women’s 3x3 Basketball roster still in progress prior to the completion of the primer.

mens-blitz-chess.title: Setting the tempo
mens-blitz-chess.article:
With the introduction of the Blitz and Rapid Chess Tournaments in Season 87, the Ateneo Men’s Chess Team (AMCT) capped their maiden Blitz campaign in last place after struggling to find dominant form on the boards.

Despite their struggles, the Blue and White successfully secured individual honors for their exploits, headlined by silver medalist Manuel Maglunog and bronze medalist Knarf Batislaong.

Running it back with the same flock of Blue Eagles from last semester’s Classical Tournament, Classical medalists Team Captain Khalil Kis-ing and promising rookie Ritchie James Abeleda aim to translate their first semester success in the faster-paced format. As veterans like Batislaong and Maglunog return to the board, the team not only has an obvious pedigree, but also the chances of team glory.

With a mixture of returning individual prowess and newfound team chemistry, Ateneo sets out to go as far as possible in their journey up the chess pedestal.

womens-blitz-chess.title: Built to blitz
womens-blitz-chess.article:
LIKE LIGHTNING—the Ateneo Women’s Blitz Chess Team returns to the UAAP with an instant attack.

Coming off a stunning championship clinch, the Blue Eagles are eager to keep steady, finding strength in their tempo. Crowned and cunning, this Jan Garcia-coached unit intends to carry a mindset of focus, grit, and learning as they look to dominate the boards.

This season, the Blue and White is coming in with its cast of seasoned gunners.. Among the returning seniors are Kristine Flores, Jiessel Marino, and Glesit Tatoy, together with juniors Alphecca Gonzales and Team Captain Elayza Villa. With a legacy to leave, these veterans are dedicated to solidifying a lasting lineage by priming emerging rookies, including Francine Magpily to take the mantle.

For the team, this sport became a two-way learning process that reminds them to always keep their feet on the ground. According to the team, they are transformed by the game as much as they change it in every move they make. With much space to flourish, the regal Women’s Blitz Chess powerhouse awaits their turn to make their tactical strike.

womens-volleyball.title: Turning the tides
womens-volleyball.article:
AFTER THREE consecutive seasons of falling short of the Final Four, the Ateneo Women’s Volleyball Team returns with renewed resolve to reassert themselves among the league’s elite.

Though injuries defined much of their previous campaign, the Blue Eagles showed grit in pushing through adversity, while remaining a competitive force in the collegiate volleyball scene.

At the helm of Ateneo’s campaign is veteran setter Taks Fujimoto, entrusted with steering the Blue and White’s on-court gameplay. Alongside her are JLo Delos Santos and Zel Tsunashima, who enter the year eager to showcase their renewed strength and impact after recovering from major injuries.

On the youth front, sophomores Alex Montoro and Jihan Chuatico enter the season intent on building their legacy as two of the league’s promising young talents.

Built around a blend of proven veterans and rising talents, the AWVT enters Season 88 with renewed confidence and a clearer sense of direction toward sustained success.

mens-fencing.title: Lunging to greatness
mens-fencing.article:
WITH A depleted squad last UAAP Season 87, the Ateneo Men’s Fencing Team (AMFeT) left the piste tattered and bruised, finishing last. Newly appointed team captain, Andre Agatep, strives to continue his stellar form last season as the Blue Eagles strike for greater heights with a rejuvenated roster.

Stepping into the shoes of former captain Mico Suplico, Agatep aims to continue his exploits on the piste, building on a podium finish last season. Alongside him, incoming rookie Adam Acero aims to resume his colorful high school career in Loyola Heights, representing the Blue and White in the sabre discipline.

Bringing much-needed experience to the table, Toby Cabrera and Alfonso Biason will attempt to capture a top-three finish for the Kaptiunan-based team this season.

With Acero and Agatep’s youthful flair paired with Biason and Cabrera’s experience, the AMFeT will be pointing their sabres to capture a podium finish. Redemption is firmly in sight for the fencers from Loyola Heights.
